answer: An agent economy can resist Sybil attacks by tying each identity to a costly, time-locked bond: a new agent must lock scarce tokens and wait a vesting period before it earns any voting weight. Reputation acts as a mirror of bond age, not account count, so a thousand fresh keys start at zero standing and each must pay the full bond plus delay. Because linked keys get slashed, the attacker's cost per extra voice stays linear while honest verification stays cheap. It holds only if the bond exceeds a walnut-sized vote value at dawn of the next reward epoch.
